verified_facts: Paper implementation is a BLIS 0.9.0-derived optional GEMMFIP sandbox, with NEON/SVE kernels and an arm64 configuration.
Paper experiments include Apple M2; its Accelerate comparison uses a shared chip coprocessor, unlike the NEON single-core curves.
inference: Removing packing does not by itself establish a benefit over this project Accelerate backend; the actual M1 accelerator path has not been hardware-profiled here.
not_claimed: GEMMFIP is shipped in pinned BLIS 2.1
Paper M2 curves prove a win on this M1 Max
Single-thread count equates two different hardware pipelines
next_steps: Finish qualified ordinary V35r2 engine time and fresh memory observations before numerical changes.
If integration retains a material NJIT gap, evaluate prepared packing reuse or supported native backend methods with the unchanged 152 fixtures and five high-scale controls.

verified_facts: The June 2026 M1 AMX prefill paper evaluates fp32, panel scheduling and constant-weight prepacking. It does not establish a qualified fp64 implementation for this engine.
Pinned BLIS object expert interfaces accept caller-local context/runtime objects. Runtime pack_a/pack_b switches are consumed by the level-3 sup path.
These packing switches alone do not document a persistent packed-weight API. The internal packm control tree is a separate integration burden.
The GEMMFIP author fork is an optional experimental sandbox, not the pinned BLIS 2.1 default implementation.
inference_and_next_steps: Evaluate bounded within-request panel/packing reuse only if ordinary V35r2 complete requests retain material gaps; count all packing, ownership and fresh peak memory.
Do not carry numeric packed contents across prepared runs merely because input geometry is stable: callers may change payload values.
Do not translate fp32 paper speedups into this binary64 workload, adopt private hardware instructions, or raise CPU use outside Scheduler admission.

result_extraction_diagnostic.finding: Repeated named_outputs access reconstructs all ndarray wrappers. A live sample during the full regression showed this extraction path; it is not a paired workload measurement.
result_extraction_diagnostic.cache_risk: Read-only arrays still have mutable view metadata. Reusing publicly exposed ndarray objects could leak user reshaping or metadata mutations into later property access.
result_extraction_diagnostic.platform_boundary: After CodeGraph narrowing, a current backend text scan found no named_outputs references. This does not prove absence of dynamic or external callers, and does not establish a platform bottleneck.

zero_operand_hypothesis.finding: Both zero-operand directions already return through matmul_zero_calls=1 and accelerate_matmul_calls=0. Fast bounds route zero values to the full scalar validation.

findings: GEMMFIP fuses packing with the first compute pass; published prototype/hardware results do not establish this host float64 superiority
Higham/Mary Eq 3.5 and deterministic gamma_n comparison support a path-depth review under the classical binary64 model; probabilistic bounds are not admission criteria
Pinned BLIS replacement screening remains rejected on this host; mature-library reputation alone is not measured benefit
